batch_strategy: Complement the pending sixteen with connected tests of amount response, endpoint-specific solvent response and transfer between related structures. Recheck two m92 boundaries where repeated-input variation now challenges apparent curvature, investigate the exceptional m207 midpoint through neighboring eluent ratios, and add independent interpolation and terminal-solvent checks. Numerical widths and distances are secondary evidence; selection targets predictive learning across the Row-distribution.

choices.reason: Measure m207 at 2/1 and 100 uL; frozen prediction 8.36/13.38 mL. Its 5/1 midpoint ec6846c0fcb7df17c97d measured 4.89/10.42, far earlier than both measured amount boundaries. This neighboring-eluent label tests whether that exceptional midpoint extends into stronger eluent, helping distinguish a localized observation from a broader response associated with the supplied conditions.

Measure m207 at 10/1 and 100 uL; frozen prediction 34.10/58.21 mL. Same-ratio high-amount record 8f5452ff0e84ab2e2057 measured 32.79/61.14. Together with the selected 2/1 midpoint, this tests the solvent dependence of the unexpectedly early 5/1 midpoint ec6846c0fcb7df17c97d without assuming that its amount-response shape generalizes.

Measure secondary benzylic alcohol m67 at 20/1 and 100 uL; frozen prediction 37.39/62.53 mL. Boundaries 2cf4f6424b85ab121943 and 80f6a235bb59c2a7ea59 measured 42.23/62.09 and 30.59/62.98. The midpoint tests curvature within a large onset contrast and nearly stable completion, extending the measured solvent-dependent contraction of its amount response.

Measure cyclopropyl beta-keto ester m94 at 20/1 and 100 uL; frozen prediction 37.93/77.68 mL. Boundaries ffc70e28db22d1cc1f3f and ffffcd6f3b9393846ab4 showed an 11.19-mL onset decline. The newly measured 10/1 panel, including 7ac90b210e42d27c5a04 and 5b445b457a8b897a2d6c, showed a smaller 5.17-mL decline. This completes the weak-eluent panel and tests whether onset curvature and completion response transfer between ratios.

Low boundary b008f92639d8bb738954 measured 8.55/15.80, and recent 10/1 midpoint d21f08a7e8eaa163ecfc measured 12.19/25.05. This supplies a new amount contrast in a related ester, testing transfer of onset contraction and completion response after the much later 50/1 observation 3fc05dc2025715e68174.

Repeat the supplied m92 10/1, 50-uL tuple; frozen prediction 8.83/23.54 mL. Low and high observations e2f15590b7142490599b and 50e113fcc37184809670 completed at 21.03 and 24.51, below the new midpoint completion of 28.15 in 4b8ba288d549f6cfc94b. Because the analogous 2/1 interpretation weakened after a boundary repeat, this label checks whether the 10/1 interior elevation has a reproducible boundary contrast.

Repeat the supplied m92 50/1, 50-uL tuple; frozen prediction 17.74/50.35 mL. Initial low record 1844eab177de5d01fab6 measured 22.57/52.44, whereas midpoint 7b42519983cf93dd7efd and high record 9bbd36c8b484b5609808 completed at 61.95 and 62.21. Rechecking the low boundary tests a rise followed by a plateau against variation unexplained by the recorded inputs.

Measure para-aminobenzonitrile m160 at 5/1 and 100 uL; frozen prediction 40.57/96.19 mL. Boundaries ad833f34f6b91872362d and fe66b2381d33aa2ea3a8 measured 44.72/101.17 and 38.93/96.66. This completes its amount panel for comparison with the measured meta-isomer panel, including 17902fa9c7f8ea9b456e, and tests interpolation in an aromatic nitrogen environment with substantial historical failures.

Measure m160 at 1/1 and 150 uL; frozen prediction 6.75/19.29 mL. This directly matches the loading conditions of meta-isomer observation f9d4d16c9703edbbe541, which measured 5.84/19.38. It also adds an amount comparison to para-isomer midpoint fbf7711e24f45bf06d4f. The matched comparison determines how much of the large measured 5/1 positional-isomer gap persists in stronger eluent.

Measure ethyl nicotinate m90 at 2/1 and 50 uL; frozen prediction 11.43/27.20 mL. Same-ratio midpoint 0460dfc4e1747f0fc92c measured 14.42/29.27. At 5/1, 855832bd4005ac7abdc6 and b51b5dbcd2a38b174973 showed earlier onset but later completion at higher amount. This new strong-eluent amount comparison tests whether those endpoint responses contract or change shape.

Measure methylthio-substituted acetophenone m128 at 10/1 and 100 uL; frozen prediction 31.61/53.66 mL. Its predicted onset lies below both measured boundaries: 39.47 in 2f72c334253bbe94a8ab and 33.83 in 596bd04bfe916866f908. This discriminates a real interior feature from an interpolation underestimate, providing an independent test of amount sensitivity outside the alcohol and beta-keto-ester families.

Measure para-nitroacetophenone m37 at 5/1 and 50 uL; frozen prediction 12.89/31.07 mL. High boundary 65f6e8326897810ec715 measured 13.10/31.19. Its 20/1 boundaries 606886b17304ec494aa0 and 3b2c663a28a9f32bd1d3 showed a 9.84-mL onset decline with a much smaller completion change. This tests whether the amount contrast contracts at 5/1 in a nitroketone.

Together with the selected high boundary, this tests the almost amount-invariant predictions against a complete local response and asks whether the onset contrast observed for related nitroketone m37 transfers to this aldehyde.

Measure m193 at 20/1 and 150 uL; frozen prediction 36.42/78.25 mL. The predicted endpoints are almost unchanged from the low-amount candidate. With the selected low boundary and measured midpoint c28747d70e7b51a1cc95, this separates endpoint slopes from an interior feature and tests structure-dependent transfer of the m37 weak-eluent amount response.

Recent CW record c0adb1c6f9dbe862a4dc measured 4.67/6.01 at 10/1, with an acquisition-time completion overestimate of 9.04 mL; 1910a349b60a38899055 measured 4.39/8.82 at 1/1. This missing terminal anchor tests the predicted completion increase and extends failure repair to a less represented structural environment.

Measure bromopropionic acid m45 at 1/1 and 100 uL; frozen prediction 8.77/14.09 mL. It bridges 22fc04337abf53335eb8 at 2/1, measured 6.84/11.64, and neat-EA observation fb031b748f1f5a8cc89e, measured 5.12/8.56. This tests a predicted strong-eluent reversal in an acid-containing compound; anomalous weak-eluent record 129036e0bccc4ff7e848 does not establish a reliable chromatographic trend.

hypotheses.content: m92 may have solvent-dependent amount curvature, but some apparent shape may be variation unexplained by the supplied inputs. The proposed 2/1 midpoint maximum is weakened; the 10/1 interior completion elevation and 50/1 rise followed by a plateau require boundary checks.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The repeated 2/1 low boundary overlaps the midpoint completion range, undermining a deterministic peak inferred from the earlier low record. Repeated boundaries at other ratios can distinguish useful conditional response shape from unsupported propagation of an exceptional label.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the 10/1 and 50/1 low boundaries reproduce their earlier completion values relative to the measured midpoint and high boundaries?

hypotheses.content: For m135 and m67, the measured onset contrast across amount boundaries contracts as EA fraction increases. Completion follows a separate response. The size and curvature of the amount association therefore need molecule- and eluent-dependent treatment.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The connected observations constrain an interaction that nearly amount-invariant predictions can miss. Intermediate labels test curvature while keeping the onset correction separate from completion.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m67's 20/1 midpoint interpolate between its widely separated onset boundaries while completion remains near the measured boundary range?

hypotheses.content: m94's onset amount contrast grows from 1/1 to 10/1 to 20/1, while completion changes much less in its measured 10/1 panel. Transfer to other beta-keto esters requires separate endpoint responses: m82's recent 5/1 low boundary shows a substantial completion difference, and m25 remains a useful ester-substituent comparison.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These common motifs provide connected tests of structure-by-eluent-by-amount relationships. They can constrain onset curvature without imposing stable completion or transferring one ester's response magnitude to every analogue.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: What is m94's 20/1 midpoint response, and does m25 show a measurable onset or completion contrast across its 5/1 amount boundaries?

hypotheses.content: The new strong-eluent m161 observation suggests contraction of the large 5/1 aminobenzonitrile positional-isomer gap, but a matched-loading comparison is still needed. In pyridine ester m90, the measured 5/1 onset decrease coexists with a completion increase; its stronger-eluent amount response remains unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched comparisons test sensitivity to nitrogen environment and substitution beyond descriptor similarity. The additional amount comparisons can prevent a shared correction from shifting V1 and V2 inappropriately.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m160 and m161 converge at matched 1/1 high loading, does m160 interpolate smoothly at 5/1, and how does m90's low-to-midpoint contrast behave at 2/1?

hypotheses.content: The earlier-onset association with higher amount observed for nitroketone m37 in weak eluent may contract at 5/1 and may transfer to para-nitrobenzaldehyde m193 at 20/1. Both extensions remain untested; the current m193 boundary predictions are essentially amount invariant.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The measurements test whether an endpoint-specific amount response generalizes beyond the alcohol and beta-keto-ester families, while distinguishing nitroketone and nitroaldehyde environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is m37's 5/1 onset contrast small, and does the complete m193 20/1 amount panel show a monotonic response, an interior feature or little association?

hypotheses.content: m207's early 5/1, 100-uL observation is an exception to smooth interpolation between its measured amount boundaries. Whether it is localized to that eluent ratio, associated more broadly with the recorded midpoint conditions, or reflects variation unexplained by the catalog is unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Automatically fitting or dismissing the exceptional midpoint could produce large errors elsewhere. Neighboring-eluent labels at the same sample volume test its scope without assuming a loading mechanism or a universal interior minimum.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 100 uL, do m207's 2/1 and 10/1 labels follow their neighboring solvent references, or are they also exceptionally early?

feedback_interpretation:
The latest outcomes support several conditional relationships while weakening smooth-response assumptions. m135's onset contrast declined from about 12.69 mL at 10/1 to 5.73 at 5/1, 2.51 at 2/1 and 0.43 at 1/1. Conversely, m67's newly measured 20/1 contrast was 11.64 mL, larger than its 10/1 and 5/1 contrasts, with little completion change across the 20/1 boundaries. These results support testing response shape rather than applying one amount correction.

m207 decisively contradicted the proposed smooth 5/1 interpolation: its midpoint measured 4.89/10.42 mL against much later boundaries. I treat this as an observed exception, not proof of a mechanism or an erroneous label, and test its scope at neighboring eluent ratios.

The repeated m92 2/1 low boundary completed at 17.03 mL, compared with 11.72 previously and midpoint completions of 17.61 and 16.82. Thus a reproducible 2/1 midpoint maximum is no longer established. The 10/1 midpoint completed above its existing boundaries, while the 50/1 midpoint nearly matched the high boundary. Two boundary checks now have more value than extending a universal peak hypothesis.

The m94 10/1 panel showed a 5.17-mL onset decline and only a 0.38-mL completion difference, supporting contraction from 20/1. However, m82's 5/1 low completion of 36.83 mL exceeded its midpoint and high completions near 29–30 mL, weakening any general claim of stable completion across beta-keto esters. m25's 10/1 result was comparatively close to its frozen prediction despite its earlier weak-eluent failure.

m161's 1/1 high-loading completion of 19.38 mL approached the measured para-isomer midpoint range, motivating a matched-loading comparison. m90's new 5/1 high boundary confirmed earlier onset but later completion relative to its midpoint. m178's neat-EA result rejected its predicted terminal completion increase; its measured solvent curve is now sufficiently anchored to pause expansion. The recent CW m27 completion overestimate motivates an independent terminal-solvent check. All errors discussed here are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale:
The sixteen supplements have no ID overlap with the pending sixteen. These choices and the pending IDs form the frozen 32-experiment batch, using the supplied full-precision premeasurement predictions; prediction values in the reasons are rounded only for readability.

The pending batch supplies broad coverage, including several nonpolar compounds and strong-eluent conditions. The supplements concentrate on relationships that isolated coverage points cannot resolve. The m207 pair investigates the largest new exceptional response. The m67 and m94 midpoints connect measured boundaries across solvent regimes, while m25 tests transfer across ester substituents. The m160 measurements connect a weak-eluent amount panel to a matched strong-eluent positional-isomer comparison, and m90 extends endpoint-specific amount testing to a pyridine ester. The nitro-compound panel tests transfer of an observed amount association across carbonyl environments. The m128 midpoint independently probes a prediction lying outside its measured onset boundary range.

Two m92 repeated-input measurements address uncertainty about which apparent response shapes are reproducible. They have specific discriminating roles following the latest contradictory boundary result. The m27 and m45 anchors add independent checks of predicted solvent-curve reversals in distinct chemical environments.

This batch may improve overall Row accuracy by constraining amount invariance, endpoint coupling, unsupported structural transfer and propagation of exceptional observations. Density times sample volume is the recorded amount feature; these comparisons establish associations rather than a loading mechanism. Missing experimental information and disagreement between identical supplied tuples limit deterministic interpretations. Quantile spans are single-predictor outputs, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and V2 minus V1 is the elution interval width.
